title: Impact of New Seed Variety Adoption on Farm Income

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Instrumental Variables (IV) / Two-Stage Least Squares (2SLS)**

**Why IV?** The adoption of a new seed variety (`x`) is likely endogenous — farmers who adopt new seeds may differ systematically from non-adopters in unobservable ways (e.g., ability, risk preferences, access to credit, soil quality not captured in controls). OLS would therefore produce biased estimates of the causal effect of adoption on income.

**Instrument:** Agroecological suitability (`z`) — a binary indicator of whether the farm's environment is suitable for the new seed variety.

**Key assumptions:**
1. **Relevance:** Agroecological suitability predicts adoption of the new seed variety (farms in suitable zones are more likely to adopt). Testable via first-stage F-statistic.
2. **Exclusion restriction:** Agroecological suitability affects farm income *only* through its effect on seed variety adoption, conditional on controls. This is plausible if `z` captures suitability specifically for the *new* variety rather than general agricultural productivity, and if `controls` captures other farm characteristics.
3. **Independence:** The instrument is as-good-as-randomly assigned conditional on controls (no selection into agroecological zones based on unobservables correlated with income).

## 2. R Code

```r
# ============================================================
# IV Analysis: Impact of New Seed Variety Adoption on Farm Income
# ============================================================

# Load required packages
if (!require("AER")) install.packages("AER", repos="http://cran.r-project.org")
if (!require("lmtest")) install.packages("lmtest", repos="http://cran.r-project.org")
if (!require("sandwich")) install.packages("sandwich", repos="http://cran.r-project.org")

library(AER)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# ---- Read Data ----
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s79_data.csv")
cat("Dataset dimensions:", nrow(df), "rows x", ncol(df), "columns\n")
cat("\nSummary statistics:\n")
print(summary(df))

# Check correlation structure
cat("\n=== Correlation Matrix ===\n")
print(round(cor(df), 4))

# ============================================================
# 1. OLS Benchmark (Naive, potentially biased)
# ============================================================
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("1. OLS REGRESSION (Benchmark)\n")
cat("========================================\n")

ols_model <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)
print(summary(ols_model))

# Robust standard errors for OLS
cat("\nOLS with Robust Standard Errors:\n")
print(coeftest(ols_model, vcov = vcovHC(ols_model, type = "HC1")))

# ============================================================
# 2. First Stage: z -> x
# ============================================================
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("2. FIRST STAGE: z -> x (Relevance Check)\n")
cat("========================================\n")

first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
print(summary(first_stage))

# First-stage F-statistic on excluded instrument
first_stage_restricted <- lm(x ~ controls, data = df)
f_test <- anova(first_stage_restricted, first_stage)
cat("\nFirst-stage F-test on excluded instrument:\n")
print(f_test)

# Manual F-stat for the instrument
coef_z <- summary(first_stage)$coefficients["z", ]
f_stat <- (coef_z["t value"])^2
cat(sprintf("\nFirst-stage F-statistic (t^2): %.2f\n", f_stat))
cat(sprintf("Rule of thumb: F > 10 indicates instrument is not weak.\n"))
if (f_stat > 10) {
  cat("=> PASS: Instrument is sufficiently strong.\n")
} else {
  cat("=> WARNING: Potential weak instrument problem.\n")
}

# ============================================================
# 3. IV / 2SLS Estimation
# ============================================================
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("3. IV / 2SLS ESTIMATION\n")
cat("========================================\n")

iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)
print(summary(iv_model, diagnostics = TRUE))

# Robust standard errors for IV
cat("\nIV with Robust Standard Errors (HC1):\n")
iv_robust <- coeftest(iv_model, vcov = vcovHC(iv_model, type = "HC1"))
print(iv_robust)

# ============================================================
# 4. Reduced Form: z -> y
# ============================================================
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("4. REDUCED FORM: z -> y\n")
cat("========================================\n")

reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = df)
print(summary(reduced_form))

# Manual Wald estimator
rf_coef <- coef(reduced_form)["z"]
fs_coef <- coef(first_stage)["z"]
wald_estimate <- rf_coef / fs_coef
cat(sprintf("\nWald (IV) estimate = Reduced Form / First Stage = %.4f / %.4f = %.4f\n",
            rf_coef, fs_coef, wald_estimate))

# ============================================================
# 5. Robustness Checks
# ============================================================
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("5. ROBUSTNESS CHECKS\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# 5a. Without controls
cat("\n--- 5a. IV without controls ---\n")
iv_no_controls <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
print(summary(iv_no_controls, diagnostics = TRUE))

# 5b. Manual 2SLS to verify
cat("\n--- 5b. Manual 2SLS verification ---\n")
x_hat <- fitted(first_stage)
manual_2sls <- lm(y ~ x_hat + controls, data = df)
cat(sprintf("Manual 2SLS coefficient on x_hat: %.4f\n", coef(manual_2sls)["x_hat"]))
cat(sprintf("ivreg coefficient on x:           %.4f\n", coef(iv_model)["x"]))

# 5c. Hausman test (endogeneity test)
cat("\n--- 5c. Hausman Test for Endogeneity ---\n")
df$resid_fs <- residuals(first_stage)
hausman_reg <- lm(y ~ x + controls + resid_fs, data = df)
hausman_p <- summary(hausman_reg)$coefficients["resid_fs", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat(sprintf("Hausman test p-value (coef on first-stage residual): %.4f\n", hausman_p))
if (hausman_p < 0.05) {
  cat("=> REJECT exogeneity: IV is preferred over OLS.\n")
} else {
  cat("=> FAIL TO REJECT exogeneity: OLS may be consistent.\n")
}

# ============================================================
# 6. Summary of Key Results
# ============================================================
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("6. SUMMARY OF KEY RESULTS\n")
cat("========================================\n")

ols_coef <- coef(ols_model)["x"]
ols_se <- summary(ols_model)$coefficients["x", "Std. Error"]
iv_coef <- coef(iv_model)["x"]
iv_se <- summary(iv_model)$coefficients["x", "Std. Error"]

cat(sprintf("OLS estimate of adoption effect:  %.4f (SE: %.4f)\n", ols_coef, ols_se))
cat(sprintf("IV  estimate of adoption effect:  %.4f (SE: %.4f)\n", iv_coef, iv_se))
cat(sprintf("First-stage F-statistic:          %.2f\n", f_stat))
cat(sprintf("Hausman test p-value:             %.4f\n", hausman_p))
cat(sprintf("\nInterpretation: A one-unit increase in seed variety adoption\n"))
cat(sprintf("causes a %.4f unit change in farm income (IV estimate).\n", iv_coef))
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Sign:** I expect a **positive** coefficient on adoption (`x`), indicating that adopting the new seed variety increases farm income. This is consistent with the premise that improved seed varieties offer higher yields or better resilience.

**Magnitude:** Looking at the data preview, `y` and `x` appear to be on similar continuous scales (roughly -2 to 2), so the IV coefficient is likely in the range of **0.5 to 1.5** — meaning a one-unit increase in adoption intensity leads to roughly a 0.5–1.5 unit increase in farm income.

**OLS vs. IV comparison:** The OLS estimate could be biased in either direction:
- **Upward bias** if more productive/wealthier farmers self-select into adoption
- **Downward bias** if adoption is driven by need (struggling farmers try new varieties)

The IV estimate will reflect the **Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE)** for compliers — farms whose adoption was driven by agroecological suitability.

**First-stage F-statistic:** I expect F > 10 since `z` (agroecological suitability) should be a meaningful predictor of adoption. The correlation between `x` and `z` in the preview appears moderate.

**Hausman test:** If endogeneity is present (as the research design assumes), the Hausman test should reject at conventional significance levels, confirming that IV is preferred over OLS.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use agroecological suitability as an instrument for new seed variety adoption.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Adopting the new seed variety leads to a significant increase in farm income.
